assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: one full side-profile game sprite and visual style sample for the Mira Grade 1 science lesson on goldfish.
Primary request: illustrate one anatomically accurate common single-tail orange goldfish (Carassius auratus), swimming level, head to the left and tail to the right. A straight lateral view, not three-quarter, so children can recognize and a game can align to the mouth, eye, gill cover, scales, and tail fin.
Subject details: a small natural mouth at the extreme left, one visible round dark eye just behind and above the mouth, a clearly readable curved gill-cover edge behind that eye, a sturdy moderately oval trunk with fine overlapping scales, a clear dorsal fin above the trunk and natural visible side and underside fins. A narrow tail base leads to one broad subtly forked tail fin on the right. Distinct silhouette and separation between eye, gill cover, scales, and tail fin. Do not expose the gills or depict any wound.
Composition: wide 16:9-friendly landscape with the single complete fish roughly 83 percent of the canvas width, centered horizontally and vertically. Allow clear padding around all fins and both ends. The picture must read instantly at tablet and phone scale.
Style: premium contemporary children's natural-history picture book, warm vermilion and golden orange with pale peach translucent fins, hand-painted colored pencil and controlled gouache, subtle paper-grain in the fish alone, crisp outer silhouette and gently modeled natural form. Quiet, fine, and playful without a human face or glossy 3D plastic.
Constraints: export the fish alone against genuinely transparent alpha. No tinted/white/checkerboard backdrop, floor, shadow, bubbles, water, plant, pond, labels, annotation, numbers, wordmarks, or second object. Keep mouth, eye, gill cover, scales and tail fin legible and entirely inside the frame.

Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: one transparent animated game specimen for Mira's first-grade aquarium observation lesson.
Primary request: paint one real common single-tail goldfish with a cream-white body and vivid vermilion-orange patches across forehead and upper flank, swimming level head to the left and tail to the right. Strict side profile for exact anatomy alignment. Whole fish visible and on its own. The young observer must see one dark eye, the small natural mouth in front of it, a distinct smooth curved gill cover edge behind the eye, scales, one dorsal fin, realistic side and underside fins, a tapered tail root, and one broad single forked tail fin.
Style: contemporary children's natural-history picture-book, warm colored pencil with controlled gouache and subtly grained painted surface, exquisite but quiet, smooth silhouette and natural proportions. Ivory with persimmon-orange patches, light apricot fins and a real dark round eye. No human expressions and no glossy 3D. Wide landscape approximately 16:9, body occupies 80–86 percent of the canvas width, centered with ample transparent breathing room around all fins.
Constraints: genuine transparent alpha, isolated fish only. No background color, water, gravel, decoration, highlights beyond the subject, cast shadow, labels, inset, watermark, or another animal. Do not expose internal gills.

Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: one transparent common carp specimen for a Grade 1 comparison game, separate from goldfish.
Primary request: paint exactly one anatomically recognizable common carp (Cyprinus carpio) in a true level side profile, facing left with tail to the right. Body noticeably longer and less round than a goldfish, an olive-grey and pale muted brass gradation, a discrete regular diamond scale pattern, natural eye and curved gill cover, a slightly downturned mouth with two very short natural mouth barbels, one relatively long dorsal fin, normal side/underside fins, and a clearly forked grey tail with tapering tail root. All anatomy readable at small size.
Style: fine contemporary children's natural-history picture book, controlled gouache and finely textured colored pencil, warm gentle natural colors and an exact clean silhouette. No glossy 3D, human face or decorative stylization.
Composition: wide 16:9 landscape, body takes about 84 percent of canvas width and is centered horizontally and vertically, generous margins beyond all fins.
Constraints: genuinely transparent alpha, isolated intact carp only. No pond, shadows, splashes, gravel, second fish, water tint, lettering, arrows, border, annotation, or watermark.

Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: a new specimen illustration only for the end-of-lesson picture assessment, separate from the game fish.
Primary request: exactly one complete pale butter-golden and apricot common single-tail goldfish, true full lateral profile facing RIGHT, with its tail on the left. Show it level with the viewer. Give it a compact oval trunk, one dark eye and a slightly parted small natural mouth at the foremost tip, a visible soft curved gill-cover edge behind the eye, a crisp pattern of fine pale gold overlapping scales, visible distinct underside fin and side fin, a neat dorsal fin, a slim tail root and one broad shallow forked tail. The fish must be detailed enough to crop legible close-ups of a single eye, patches of scales, the tail and the underside fin at phone scale.
Style: premium contemporary children's natural-history colored-pencil and controlled gouache, subtle grain on the fish, accurate but friendly, warm yellow-cream to apricot, distinct from a saturated orange specimen. No black outlines or comic personality.
Composition: wide 16:9 landscape, the entire right-facing fish isolated at center, about 80–85 percent of canvas width with explicit clear margins past every fin.
Constraints: preserve genuinely transparent alpha. No water, backdrop, shadow, plant, bubble, labels, arrows, numbers, boxes, inset cards, logo, watermark, separate object, or extra fish. Do not expose internal gills.

Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: one wide 16:9 empty aquarium background for an interactive first-grade fish observation game.
Primary request: paint the interior of a real freshwater observation aquarium seen straight through the front glass, at the height of a fish. Keep the middle broad, quiet, and very clear because an orange goldfish sprite and a movable camera will be layered over it separately.
Scene/backdrop: clean pale mint and cool aqua water, extremely soft natural daylight from above, a few understated round pebbles along the lowest tenth, a small cluster of healthy soft green aquatic leaves in the far left corner and one short cluster in the far right corner. Decorations must hug the extreme side and bottom edges. The central 75 percent horizontally and central 75 percent vertically is a smooth, light, open field of clear water with almost no detail, no strong caustic line, no glare streak, and no vertical divisions. No tank stand or thick glass frame.
Style/medium: contemporary fine children's natural-history picture-book art, hand-painted controlled gouache and colored-pencil texture, understated paper grain, calm clear shapes, finely rendered soft plant edges and restrained color. Pale blue-green and sea-glass mint create an easy-to-read background behind a saturated vermilion-orange fish. No 3D plastic look, no black corners or heavy vignette.
Composition/framing: 16:9 landscape; compose so narrow cropping at left/right or at the top/bottom keeps the center empty and readable. 
Constraints: this is only the backdrop, with no fish, other animals, people, food, words, numbers, arrows, labels, logos, borders, watermark, or diagram elements. No fake transparent checkerboard. Fill the image with the pale aquarium environment; the foreground character and controls are separate.

Use case: scientific-educational. Produce one landscape 16:9 illustration for the first-grade Mira lesson on observing goldfish. Use a premium contemporary children's natural-history picture-book style: controlled hand-painted gouache and colored-pencil grain, true-to-life anatomy, warm vermilion and gold fish, softly lit celadon and aquamarine clean water. Educational detail must read clearly at 160 pixels wide, with strong focal hierarchy. Show one healthy common single-tail orange goldfish, head toward the left and tilted only slightly upwards so the front mouth and one eye are unambiguous; depict it actually taking one tiny dry brown food pellet into the open mouth. This image is the instant the single clearly legible rounded pellet, about one third of the eye's diameter, touches the lower lip and crosses the visible mouth opening; keep the pellet and mouth visibly distinct, with unobstructed pale water immediately to the left of its mouth. Arrange the lips near the left-of-center third, fish's eye to their upper right, and the gill cover behind the eye. The fish head fills about half the composition and the body continues right, with a clear suggestion of its true body rather than crowded details. Let soft cyan water extend above the fish, with only subtle far background texture. No fingers, feeder, people, second fish, repeated food, arrows, text, labels, bubbles near the mouth, human-like expression, mouth inside the eye, wide human teeth, strong vignette or aquarium glass across the mouth. Compose this as a beautiful clear lateral close-up, distinct from a game sprite, with the natural gesture of gentle feeding understandable without words.

Use case: scientific-educational. One square 1:1 anatomy close-up for Mira Grade 1 on observing a living goldfish breathe. Children's natural-history picture-book illustration in controlled hand-painted gouache and delicate colored-pencil grain, healthy orange and apricot common goldfish, flat pale celadon water behind. Draw a crisp true left-facing lateral view of one healthy goldfish head and front shoulder. The full continuous contour from the fish's closed little mouth at the left to a hint of scales and a small side fin at the right must read as one living fish. Its visible round eye is above and to the left of the gill cover. At the center of the frame a narrow curved seam behind the eye is opened just a few millimeters, showing a thin shaded gap behind the curved operculum (gill cover) and making the lower free edge especially clear. The highlighted biological focal point is that naturally lifting hinged cover, larger in the composition than the eye, with a close view of the intact outer edge and a softly contrasting body just behind it. No exposed gill filaments, internal anatomy, blood or red gap, instruments, arrows, rings, anatomical cutaway, other fish, bubbles obscuring the edge, labels, text, humans, or extra anatomy. Make the seam recognizable at phone scale without exaggerating the size of the opening; show the gill cover as part of the head behind the eye, never depict it as a fin. Clean quiet watery color, expressive living subject but no human face.

Use case: scientific-educational illustration for Mira Grade 1, one landscape 16:9 picture-book illustration for children to explore an environment by looking systematically from left to right. High-quality colored pencil with gentle gouache, subtle warm paper grain and natural soft daylight; toasted cream classroom, teal green plant, celadon-blue water, warm orange goldfish. Straight-on eye-level view of a single uncluttered broad wooden observation tabletop with a clean visual division at the middle. In the LEFT half arrange exactly one leafy green non-flowering potted plant near the far left and exactly one open book with blank cream pages lying flat toward center-left, with enough clear space to search around them. There are no animals of any kind on the left. In the RIGHT half show a wide freestanding rectangular clear glass aquarium on the same table, all four edges, obvious glass boundary and visible waterline, containing exactly one easily visible orange common goldfish in profile, centrally lit and substantial in size. Place the goldfish visibly within the tank with clear glass and water all around it; child can tell it is behind the glass. Very simple tank with one subtle low green aquatic plant and a few smooth stones, no reflection that resembles a second fish. No humans, silhouettes, animals or animal prints outside the tank, other furniture dominating the composition, pets, insects, extra aquariums, writing, letters, arrows, annotation, labels or borders. Preserve three clearly readable objects and their positions at small-screen size. The book and potted plant must each be visible and separable, and the only orange and only animal is the living fish at the right. A warm inviting observation station, beautiful visual clarity suitable for printed children's science books.

Use case: scientific-educational. Make one square 1:1 picture-only assessment choice for the Mira first-grade goldfish lesson. A pale butter-gold common goldfish in exact side view, head faces RIGHT. A crisp close-up of the head shows its naturally open little front mouth at the extreme right profile, with visible upper and lower lips framing a modest dark opening in the RIGHT CENTER of the image. Its eye is behind and a little higher to the LEFT, and only partly prominent; the real anatomical opening is the unmistakable focus. Show gentle yellow and peach scales, minimal hints of the rest of the head. Use premium traditional colored-pencil and light gouache natural-history children's art, with restrained hand-painted texture and a simple pale mint aquatic background; clear silhouette, accurate visual distinction between mouth and eye at a very small phone option card. No food, no hands, no arrow or text, no glyph, no circle surrounding the mouth, no visible teeth, no exaggerated human expression, no anthropomorphism, no mechanical gills, no vertical abstract section. Include breathing space to the right so the silhouette of both lips is clean and not cropped.

Use case: educational picture-only multiple-choice illustration. Produce one square 1:1 picture for the Mira Grade 1 goldfish lesson. Premium children's natural-history picture-book style, traditional controlled colored pencil and gouache, clear visual story, warm cream wood and celadon classroom. In the lower left half show one first-grade-aged East Asian child with short dark hair in a warm ochre long-sleeved sweater, side three-quarter view facing right, sitting on a low stool looking closely at one orange goldfish inside a rectangular clear open-top aquarium that occupies the right half. The child is quietly observing behind the glass and recording on an open paper sketchbook laid on the tabletop to the LEFT of the glass aquarium, resting one hand on the open notebook and holding one visible pencil in the other hand touching the page. Draw the gentle drawing action as clear as the goldfish, including both hands and sketchbook at phone scale. The hands, child's head, and pencil are all visibly separated from the glass by clear empty space. Show the calm clear waterline and one healthy fish, with unobtrusive props only and no activity lines. No visible writing, letters, arrows, praise mark, checkmark, symbols, speech bubble, tapping or reaching gesture, second fish, smiling at the viewer or text of any kind. Keep all important visible things inside the center 90 percent so the card can be read without words at 100px wide.

Image edit, one square educational picture choice. Keep the reference illustration's premium gouache-and-colored-pencil style, schoolchild's identity and ochre sleeve, exactly one orange fish inside a rectangular clear aquarium on the right, and the warm tabletop and cream/celadon environment. Change the schoolchild's action and the position of the hands only: the child leans forward and deliberately raises one CLOSED FIST at about shoulder height, beside the OUTER vertical glass side of the aquarium, as if about to tap it. Make this fist large and fully visible around the image center, with a narrow gap between the knuckles and the outside glass edge. Add just two short gently painted motion strokes behind the wrist aimed toward the glass to communicate the movement, no symbols or graphic overlays otherwise. Keep that hand well below the aquarium rim and entirely in air, never behind glass or in water, with the vertical front corner and waterline both visible. The other hand is still on the open sketchbook on the table, with the pencil set down on the page, so it is unmistakable the child has paused drawing. Keep the tank and child's hand equally clear at 100 pixels wide. Preserve gentle lighting, palette and the framing, and keep the fish healthy and inside. No hands over the tank, no submerged hand, no cracked glass, dangerous action beyond the illustrated gesture, arrows, text, words, warning or cross sign, second child or living fish.

Image edit, one square educational picture choice. Keep the reference's schoolchild with dark hair and ochre sweater, traditional colored-pencil gouache style, same right-hand rectangular clear open aquarium with one healthy goldfish, and warm cream tabletop. Change the pose clearly: the child leans up over the open top from left to right, with ONE long ochre-sleeved arm reaching across the UPPER RIM and curving DOWN through the visible blue-green WATER SURFACE. The child has rolled the sleeve of the one reaching arm just to above the wrist. Show that one complete reaching hand and its downward fingers truly SUBMERGED a little below the surface, as seen through the FRONT glass inside the tank. Draw small natural concentric ripples right where that wrist breaks the waterline, and include both dry arm above the water and bluish tinted submerged hand below it so the visual distinction is obvious at 100 pixels wide. Put the clear fingers in water at least a good distance to the left or above the living fish, no contact. Keep the child's OTHER hand flat on the table with pencil set aside and a little open sketchbook lower left. Ensure the hand is visible through transparent glass, not crossed by opaque rim, obscured or floating outside the tank. Maintain consistent setting and camera, the crisp centered hand action is the visual key. No fist near the outside glass, no banging or splashing, no grabbing a fish, no text, no arrows or marks, no second child or living fish.
